reason: The cited code invokes a fixed GitPython `repo.git.branch(...)` operation and returns its output; these lines do not show arbitrary host code execution, only a constrained git branch command. It reads and returns branch information from a local `git.Repo`, which is host repository data and may be non-public, so SECRET is supported. It does not send data to any external/attacker-readable destination, only returns `TextContent` to the caller, so SINK is not supported. The returned text can include user-influenced content, e.g. an invalid `branch_type` is echoed directly and branch names in the repo may be attacker-controlled, so UNTRUSTED is supported.
